new_scholarship.name: Exemption from Tuition Fees for International Students (Heidelberg University Charter of 28 July 2017)
new_scholarship.official_source: Heidelberg University (Universität Heidelberg) — Central Administration, Management of Studies
new_scholarship.duration: Exemption normally runs for the standard period of study (Regelstudienzeit) of the degree programme; typically three years / six semesters for a Heidelberg Bachelor's programme
new_scholarship.deadline: The application for exemption must have reached the University by 15 July of a year for the winter semester and by 15 January of a year for the summer semester (Ausschlussfrist, an exclusion deadline). The official page states: 'The application deadline for exemption from tuition fees in accordance with Heidelberg University's regulations is 15 July for the following winter semester and 15 January for the following summer semester.'
new_scholarship.application_period: Two rounds a year, aligned to the semester cycle: applications for the following winter semester run to 15 July, applications for the following summer semester run to 15 January (date of receipt). Where the application period for the chosen degree programme closes before 15 July or 15 January (for example for Master's programmes), the exemption application may instead be submitted together with the admission application. Decisions are notified in August for the winter round and in March for the summer round.
application_method: Separate application by the student — this exemption is NOT granted automatically on admission
Download and complete the official form 'Application for exemption from tuition fees for international students in accordance with the Heidelberg University charter of 28 July 2017'
Scan the completed and signed form together with all verifying documents and send them electronically, preferably as PDF, to studiengebuehren@zuv.uni-heidelberg.de
If the admission application for the chosen degree programme closes before 15 July / 15 January, submit the exemption application together with the admission application instead
No separate online portal is published for the exemption itself
new_scholarship.description: Heidelberg University exempts international first-semester students from the Baden-Württemberg international tuition fee on grounds of special aptitude (besondere Begabung), under § 6 paras. 4 and 5 of the State Higher Education Fees Act (Landeshochschulgebührengesetz, LHGebG) and the Heidelberg University charter of 28 July 2017. Universities may exempt up to 5% of their international first-semester students, wholly or in part; the Ministry of Science, Research and the Arts fixes the maximum number for the study year and the Rectorate fixes the number per semester. Eligible applicants must submit a separate application by 15 July for the following winter semester or by 15 January for the following summer semester. Selection is made by the Central Admission Committee of the Senate for International Students, which also decides whether the exemption is full or partial; where applications exceed the quota, social criteria and equality aspects are applied, with particular consideration for students from African, Caribbean and Pacific states or least developed countries.
new_scholarship.best_fit: Non-EU/EEA applicants holding, or about to hold, admission or enrolment in a Heidelberg Bachelor's or State Examination programme, whose secondary school results and achievements go beyond the normal Abitur grade, who can document awards, prizes, scholarships or other distinctions, and who can finance their own living costs while seeking remission of the EUR 1,500 per semester international tuition fee.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Eligibility is defined by fee liability under § 2 LHGebG rather than by a nationality list: students who are not citizens of an EU or EEA member state (European Economic Area: Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway) and who hold a foreign university entrance qualification are liable for the tuition fee and may apply. The applicant must be enrolled, or about to be enrolled, at Heidelberg University at the start of the approval period in a fundamental (undergraduate) Bachelor's, State Examination or consecutive Master's programme, and must demonstrate special aptitude: proven school and/or academic achievements exceeding the normal Abitur grade, special distinctions awarded on performance criteria, or prizes or scholarships. EU/EEA nationals and international students holding a German university entrance qualification are already exempt from the fee.

new_scholarship.selection_notes: Selection is made by the Central Admission Committee of the Senate of Heidelberg University for International Students, which also decides whether the exemption is full or partial. The charter publishes no numerical weighting: the primary test is demonstrated special aptitude (besondere Begabung) evidenced by school and/or academic achievements exceeding the normal Abitur grade, special distinctions awarded on performance criteria, or prizes or scholarships. Where the number of applications with demonstrated special aptitude exceeds the exhaust number fixed by the Rectorate for the semester, selection takes place with regard to social criteria and equality aspects (§ 4 para. 2 of the charter). Students from African, Caribbean and Pacific states or among the least developed countries are given particular consideration (§ 4 para. 3). No interview and no portfolio are required.
new_scholarship.notes: Official scheme name is taken from the official application form and the charter; the German charter title is recorded in research_notes as the authoritative name. No acronym exists, so no short_title is supplied (the v2 schema has no short_title key). This is a tuition-fee exemption, not a stipend: no living allowance, travel grant, installation support or insurance is published. The exemption is granted by the committee in full or in part; the university publishes no percentage or partial-amount schedule, so the actual remission of a partial award is unknowable in advance. The EUR 1,500 per semester waiver value is the published Baden-Württemberg international tuition fee, not a separate stipend figure. No exact calendar deadline date is published, so deadline_date is null and the recurring 15 July / 15 January rule is quoted in the deadline field. No timezone is published for the deadline; the university is in Germany so German local time applies in practice, but this is not stated officially. No age limit, gender restriction, bond, service obligation or repayment obligation is published. The same charter also covers consecutive Master's programmes; this record is filed at bachelor's level as assigned, and the Master's coverage is recorded in programme_detail_official.degree_levels and in research_notes. The university notes that only the German version of its fee information forms is legally binding. The English web pages carry copyright '©2026 Heidelberg University' and the application form download carries an upload date of 2025-03-25.

programme_detail_official.application_cycle: Two application rounds a year. Winter semester round: application must reach the University by 15 July of the year (for the following winter semester). Summer semester round: by 15 January of the year (for the following summer semester). As at the verification date of 2026-10-03 the live round is the summer semester round (deadline 15 January 2027). Decisions are notified in August for the winter round and in March for the summer round.
programme_detail_official.deadline_central_display: 15 July for the following winter semester and 15 January for the following summer semester (date of receipt; Ausschlussfrist, an exclusion deadline).
programme_detail_official.deadline_note: No exact calendar date is published. The charter (§ 2) and the official application form both state the recurring rule only: the application must have reached the University by 15 July of a year for the winter semester and by 15 January of a year for the summer semester. No year is attached to either date on any official page, so deadline_date is null rather than a derived date. No timezone is published; the university is located in Germany and processes the deadline as a German domestic date of receipt, but this is not stated officially and is not recorded as a fact. Where the application period for the chosen degree programme closes before 15 July or 15 January, the exemption application may be submitted together with the admission application instead, and individual exemption decisions then follow only after the general deadline.
programme_detail_official.status_note: This is a standing, recurring scheme under § 6 paras. 4 and 5 LHGebG and the Heidelberg University charter of 28 July 2017, with a live application round for the summer semester (deadline 15 January 2027 as at 2026-10-03). It has run since the winter semester 2017/18 and there is no published end date. The winter-semester round for 2027/28 opens to applications now and closes on 15 July 2027.
programme_detail_official.funding_duration: Exemption normally applies for the standard period of study (Regelstudienzeit) of the degree programme; the university's own illustrative figure for a Bachelor's programme is six semesters (three years), for which it estimates EUR 9,000 of tuition in total.
programme_detail_official.tuition_coverage_note: The waived item is the international student tuition fee of EUR 1,500 per semester imposed by Baden-Württemberg on international students for Bachelor's, State Examination and consecutive Master's programmes. The committee decides whether the exemption is full or partial, and the university publishes no percentage or reduced-amount schedule, so a partial remission cannot be quantified in advance. The non-waivable semester contribution of EUR 189.80 per semester (2026/27 winter semester) is not covered and remains payable by all students of all nationalities. Accordingly the award is tuition-only and fully_funded is false.
programme_detail_official.funding_label: Exemption from the EUR 1,500 per semester international student tuition fee (full or partial), normally for the standard period of study of the degree programme; no living allowance, travel grant or other support, and the EUR 189.80 per semester semester contribution remains payable.

programme_detail_official.citizenship_residency: Eligibility is defined by fee liability rather than by a list of nationalities. The university states that international students from non-EU and non-EEA countries (European Economic Area: Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway) with a foreign university entrance qualification are required to pay the EUR 1,500 per semester tuition fee, and that students from EU and EEA member states as well as international students with a German university entrance qualification are exempt from it. No residence-in-Germany requirement is published for this exemption. Swiss nationals are not named separately on the English page.
programme_detail_official.international_eligibility: Open to all non-EU/non-EEA nationalities with a foreign university entrance qualification; the scheme exists precisely because such students are the fee-liable group. Junior ERASMUS Mundus masters students do not apply: junior doctoral students pay no fee. Where applications exceed the exhaust number, students from African, Caribbean and Pacific states or among the least developed countries are given particular consideration under § 6 para. 4 sentence 2 LHGebG.
programme_detail_official.application_method: Separate written application by the student on the university's prescribed form, submitted electronically as a PDF to studiengebuehren@zuv.uni-heidelberg.de. There is no online portal and no postal route published for the exemption itself. The application is not automatic on admission and is not part of the degree programme admission decision.
programme_detail_official.application_route: Download and complete the official form, attach the passport or identity document copy, the admission or enrolment evidence and the special-aptitude evidence, then scan and email the signed package as a PDF to studiengebuehren@zuv.uni-heidelberg.de by 15 July (following winter semester) or 15 January (following summer semester), as a date-of-receipt deadline. Where the degree programme's own application period closes earlier, submit the exemption application together with the admission application instead.

selection_weighting.note: The charter publishes no numerical weighting. The operative test is demonstrated special aptitude; social criteria and equality aspects operate only as ranking factors where the number of qualifying applications exceeds the exhaust number fixed by the Rectorate for the semester.

programme_detail_official.duration: Exemption normally applies for the standard period of study (Regelstudienzeit) of the degree programme. The university's published cost estimate for a six-semester Bachelor's programme implies three years / six semesters as the typical standard period for a Heidelberg Bachelor's degree.
award_holder_conditions: The exemption ends when the student is no longer liable for the fee under §§ 2 ff. LHGebG

The exemption ends on successful completion of the higher education studies or of the programme for which it was granted, at the latest with the close of the second month after the month in which the last examination component was taken (§ 6 para. 2 b) of the charter)
The exemption ends on early termination of the studies by change of subject, dropping out or deregistration (§ 6 para. 2 c) of the charter)
The exemption can be revoked or withdrawn because of false statements (§ 6 para. 3) of the charter)
The applicant must inform the International Relations Office immediately of any changes to the information provided in the application
Providing negligent or deliberately false information is an administrative offence and can lead to exclusion from the procedure or to later revocation of the exemption
The semester contribution of EUR 189.80 per semester remains payable in full throughout the exemption
Where a partial exemption is granted, the student must pay the remaining part of the tuition fee

§ 6 LHGebG exemptions: leave of absence under § 61 LHG, practical year under § 1 para. 2 clause 1 no. 1 ÄApprO, and practical semester under § 29 para. 3 clause 2 LHG — for the duration of the reason
§ 7 LHGebG waiver for financial emergency through no fault of the applicant's own; not available to students in their first semester

§ 22 para. 2 LGebG waiver for undue hardship, e.g. unexpected additional re-registration after cancelled examinations or inability to earn credits due to documented closure of laboratories or childcare/school closures
Heidelberg University charter quota exemption for special aptitude (this record)
BAföG, the Studierendenwerk student loan route and the KfW-Studienkredit are published by the university as separate financing options

programme_detail_official.description: Under § 6 paras. 4 and 5 of the State Higher Education Fees Act (Landeshochschulgebührengesetz, LHGebG) and the Heidelberg University charter of 28 July 2017, Heidelberg University exempts international first-semester students from the EUR 1,500 per semester international tuition fee on grounds of special aptitude. The Ministry of Science, Research and the Arts fixes the maximum number of exemptions for the study year and the Rectorate fixes the number per semester, within the statutory ceiling of up to 5% of international first-semester students. Applicants must make a separate written application by 15 July for the following winter semester or 15 January for the following summer semester. The Central Admission Committee of the Senate for International Students decides the award and whether it is full or partial. Where applications exceed the exhaust number, social criteria and equality aspects are applied, with particular consideration for students from African, Caribbean and Pacific states or among the least developed countries.
programme_detail_official.coverage: Exemption from the international student tuition fee of EUR 1,500 per semester, in full or in part, normally for the standard period of study of the degree programme. The EUR 189.80 per semester semester contribution (2026/27 winter semester), living costs, travel, accommodation, insurance and installation are not covered. The university states that living costs of the kind implied by the EUR 992 minimum monthly cost of living it publishes for visa purposes generally cannot be met by a part-time job alone.

application_readiness_checklist: You are not a citizen of an EU or EEA member state (European Economic Area: Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway)
You hold a foreign university entrance qualification, which is what makes you liable for the EUR 1,500 per semester fee
You hold, or expect to hold, a letter of admission or certificate of enrolment for a Heidelberg Bachelor's or State Examination programme
You have evidence of school and/or academic achievements going beyond your normal Abitur grade
You have documents for any special distinctions awarded on performance criteria, prizes or scholarships
You have a passport or identity document page showing your name in Latin script
If relevant, you have drafted the optional written explanation of at most two DIN A4 pages on your social circumstances
Every document not in German or English has a sworn or officially authorised translation with the translator's original stamp and signature
You have scanned the completed, signed form and all verifications into a single PDF
You are emailing to studiengebuehren@zuv.uni-heidelberg.de well before 15 July (winter semester) or 15 January (summer semester), because it is a date-of-receipt deadline
You can still fund the EUR 189.80 semester contribution, your living costs and your health insurance out of pocket
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 15 July or 15 January date-of-receipt deadline, which the charter calls an Ausschlussfrist (exclusion deadline)
Not attaching the letter of admission or certificate of enrolment, which the charter makes a mandatory attachment
Submitting documents in a language other than German or English, or translations not made by a sworn or officially authorised translator
Assuming the award is automatic on admission and never submitting the separate application
Applying while holding an EU/EEA nationality or a German university entrance qualification, which already exempts you from the fee
Relying only on a good final grade without exceeding it, when the charter asks for achievements beyond the normal Abitur grade
Expecting to keep the exemption after changing subject, dropping out or deregistering
Forgetting that the EUR 189.80 semester contribution is never waived and that living costs are entirely on you
estimated_uncovered_costs: Semester contribution: EUR 189.80 per semester (2026/27 winter semester), payable by all students of all nationalities and never waived

Living costs: the university publishes approximately EUR 992 per month as the German Embassy minimum cost of living for visa purposes, and about EUR 35,700 for a six-semester Bachelor's programme excluding tuition
Rent: approximately EUR 350 (student housing) to EUR 950 (private market) per month in Heidelberg
Health insurance: approximately EUR 150 per month, rising to approximately EUR 300 for those over 30
Public transport: EUR 45 to EUR 63 per month (Deutschlandticket)
Food, clothing and leisure: approximately EUR 150 to EUR 300 per month
Any part of the tuition fee left uncovered if the committee grants only a partial exemption, at an amount the university does not publish
document_audit: Application form: both pages, completed and signed, with place and date
Passport or identity card: the page with the name in Latin script, legible
Admission evidence: letter of admission or certificate of enrolment naming the degree programme and the intended qualification
Special-aptitude evidence: school reports, final examination results, award or prize documentation, scholarship confirmation letters
Optional social statement: at most two DIN A4 pages
Translations: sworn or officially authorised translator's original stamp and signature on each translated document
File handling: send as PDF by email; the university states electronic submission is preferred

alerts.trigger: You have just received your Heidelberg admission offer
alerts.message: Check immediately whether your programme's application period closed before 15 July or 15 January. If it did, you must file the exemption application together with your admission application, and decisions then come only after the general deadline (August for the winter round, March for the summer round).

alerts.trigger: The deadline is within a few weeks
alerts.message: Send the package now as a single PDF. The deadline is a date-of-receipt deadline, not a postmark deadline, and the charter calls it an Ausschlussfrist, so late submissions are excluded regardless of merit.

alerts.trigger: You have already paid the tuition fee for the semester in question
alerts.message: File the exemption application anyway; a successful application leads to a refund of the fee for the relevant semester. But do not assume payment will be undone automatically, and note that under the separate § 7 LHGebG hardship route a refund is impossible once the fee has been transferred for the following re-registration semester.

alerts.trigger: Your documents are not in German or English
alerts.message: Get sworn or officially authorised translations with the translator's original stamp and signature before submitting. Uncertified or unauthorised translations are the avoidable failure mode here.

alerts.trigger: You are counting on the waiver to fund your living costs
alerts.message: It will not. The exemption covers tuition only and the EUR 189.80 per semester semester contribution stays. Secure a blocked account or other proof of financial resources for the visa first; the university states these costs generally cannot be met by a part-time job alone.

alerts.trigger: You are considering changing subject or programme during your studies
alerts.message: The exemption ends on early termination of the studies by change of subject, dropping out or deregistration. Decide the subject before you rely on continued exemption.

alerts.trigger: Your circumstances change after you are awarded the exemption
alerts.message: Inform the International Relations Office immediately, as the application form requires. The exemption can be revoked for false statements, so an undeclared change is worse than a declared one.

submission_workflow: Confirm you are non-EU/EEA with a foreign university entrance qualification and therefore fee-liable
Obtain your letter of admission or certificate of enrolment for the Heidelberg programme
Assemble the special-aptitude evidence: above-average school and academic results, distinctions, prizes, scholarships
Draft the optional written explanation of social circumstances if you want them considered
Have all non-German/English documents translated by a sworn or officially authorised translator
Complete and sign the official application form, filling in your student number and the intended qualification
Scan the signed form and every verification into a single PDF
Email the package to studiengebuehren@zuv.uni-heidelingen.de by 15 July (winter semester) or 15 January (summer semester)
Keep the fee payment on schedule while you wait, since an application does not release you from the payment obligation
Expect the electronic decision in August (winter round) or March (summer round), and expect a refund of any fee already paid if the exemption is granted

research_notes.degree_level_confirmed: The Heidelberg University charter § 1 para. 2 states that students in grundständigen Studien- und Masterstudiengängen (fundamental, i.e. undergraduate, study programmes and Master's programmes) who are enrolled, or will be enrolled, at Heidelberg University at the start of the approval period and are liable for the fee under § 2 LHGebG may apply. The official application form has a tick box 'Intended qualification: Bachelor / State exam / Master's (consecutive)' and a field for the degree programme, and the tuition fee page states the fee applies for Bachelor's/Staatsexamen and consecutive Master's degree programmes. The waiver therefore funds a bachelor's degree and this record is filed at bachelor's level.
research_notes.award_selection_rationale: Four German candidates were compared. The University of Tübingen publishes only automatic statutory exceptions and hardship-based applications (Befreiungen) on its fees pages, with no charter-based quota waiver and no merit-based selection procedure. The University of Freiburg publishes statutory exclusion and exemption forms tied to § 3 and § 6 LHGebG with no university charter, no exhaust number and no selecting committee. Heidelberg was selected as the best-documented award because it publishes all of the following on its own domains: a named university charter of 28 July 2017 setting out scope, deadline, form, evidence, selection body and duration in seven numbered paragraphs; an official English application form naming the exact attachments and the mailing address; the statutory ceiling of up to 5% of international first-semester students with the Ministry and Rectorate fixing the exhaust number; the selecting committee by name; the full-or-partial decision rule; the ranking tie-breaks including ACP and least-developed-country consideration; and the EUR 1,500 per semester fee being waived, together with the EUR 189.80 semester contribution that is not.

research_notes.partial_funding_note: This is a tuition-fee exemption only, so it is not fully funded. The waived item is the EUR 1,500 per semester international tuition fee, and the committee may grant it only in part, with no published schedule for partial amounts. No living allowance, travel grant, accommodation support, insurance or installation allowance is published. The EUR 189.80 per semester semester contribution remains payable in full. The university itself publishes approximately EUR 992 per month as the minimum cost of living for visa purposes and approximately EUR 35,700 for a six-semester Bachelor's programme excluding tuition, which is the scale of the self-funded obligation.
